candidates.source_claim: For n≥2, Δ is both the left lcm and right lcm of the Artin atoms σ₁,…,σₙ₋₁. Its left divisors and right divisors coincide and are exactly the n! simple braids indexed by Sₙ. For n≤1, the positive monoid is trivial and Δ=1.
candidates.diagram_kind: paired left/right divisibility-order schematic around Δ
candidates.why_warranted: A paired schematic could help readers compare two order conventions and see that the atom family has the same least common multiple Δ on either side, while the left- and right-divisor sets of Δ agree. This is a compact optional aid for an order-heavy statement; the rendered prose and proof are already clear, so the candidate remains uncertain.
concrete_content_to_draw_or_check: For n≥2, show the atoms σ₁,…,σₙ₋₁ as elements below Δ in separate left and right divisibility-order panels; label Δ as the left lcm in one panel and right lcm in the other.
Define the order-arrow meaning in the picture: a≼L b means b=a·c, so a is a left divisor; a≼R b means b=c·a, so a is a right divisor.
If illustrating part (c), mark that the sets of elements dividing Δ on the left and on the right agree and are {σ̂:σ∈Sₙ}; do not imply that every left/right comparison in the monoid agrees.
Include the n=2 case as one atom σ₁ and Δ=σ₁, or state beside the generic schematic that the n=2 posets collapse to the single atom/top element (with identity below if shown).
If edge cases n≤1 are shown, depict the empty atom family and the trivial monoid with Δ=1 separately; do not force an atom-to-Δ diagram onto these cases.
correctness_checks: Left divisibility has factorization Δ=σ_i R_i when σ_i is a left divisor; right divisibility has Δ=L_i σ_i when σ_i is a right divisor.
The source states Δ=σ₁∨L⋯∨Lσₙ₋₁ and Δ=σ₁∨R⋯∨Rσₙ₋₁; do not reverse either lcm label.
The left and right divisor sets of Δ coincide, but the source does not assert that the left and right divisibility orders coincide on all pairs.
For n=2, there is one atom σ₁ and the triangular half-twist word has length N=1, hence Δ=σ₁; n≤1 instead has an empty alphabet, trivial monoid, and Δ=1.
A lattice/order schematic illustrates the divisibility claims; it is not a geometric crossing diagram and should not introduce an unsupported crossing or endpoint convention.
candidates.why_not_confirmed: No mathematical or rendering defect was observed. The diagram is optional explanatory support, not a repair required by the screenshot or proof.
